newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Days Inn to triple hotel rooms in Israel.
newsitem.headline: Days Inn to triple hotel rooms in Israel.

text.p: Days Inn Israel plans to nearly triple the number of hotel rooms under its franchise to 2,000 by the year 2000, Days Inn Israel president Raphael Farber said on Wednesday.
Days Inn Israel, which owns the contractual rights to the Days Inn franchise in Israel, the West Bank and Gaza Strip, has recently added a Tel Aviv hotel to its chain.
It now has six hotels in Israel and one hotel in Gush Katif, an Israeli settlement in the Palestinian-controlled Gaza Strip, with a total of 710 rooms.
Days Inn Israel pays the U.S. company, which is controlled by HFS Inc of the United States, for the licence as well as a percentage of the turnover generated by the Israeli hotels.
It owns the Days Inn hotel in Jerusalem and is building three more, two in Jerusalem and one in Eilat, with a total of 850 rooms. It is also expanding a hotel it owns in Tiberias.
All together the company is investing about $70 million in its own hotels, Farber said.
A downturn in tourism in the wake of a faltering peace process has caused occupancy rates to fall by about 10 percent at most of the Days Inn Israel hotels.
Yet Farber is going ahead with the expansion, betting that celebrations of the millenium in the year 2000 will bring five million tourists to the Holy Land.
"Tourism in Israel is cyclical. Just a year and a half ago it was the best time ever and every high point brings more tourists," he said.
"If the peace process goes ahead, tourism will flourish."
Days Inn Israel is in talks with Palestinian investors about building hotels in Jericho and Ramallah.
The company also has the right of first refusal to develop Days Inn hotels in Greece, Cyprus and Egypt. "We are beginning to negotiate that," he said.

Days Inn is not alone in its expansion in the region. Israel Land Development Co just opened four Howard Johnson hotels in Israel and plans to double the number of rooms it manages under the name to 1,200 by the end of the year.
Howard Johnson, like Days Inn, is controlled by HFS.
Farber said that at this stage the competition was welcome.

"The more international companies that come, the more consciousness will be raised among hotel owners of the need to belong to chains. In Safed (in northern Israel) the first hotel chain is Howard Johnson. So now the hotel across the street will want to become a Days Inn."
